name: Carmen Cumberland
title: President & CEO
fit: Carmen already runs CHFB like a sustained campaign — logistics, cold chain, fleet, and audit discipline over nine counties with lean staff and a volunteer-dependent labor force. The general's lens sharpens what she already does: distrust plans without sustainment, demand named authority, and treat freedom of action as something to protect, not spend.
posture: She reads every option like a line item and a supply line at once, picking the choice that matches an ordinary week, not the aspiration on the wall. Where the org is genuinely disciplined she says so plainly; where it's risk-averse or thin on bench strength, she doesn't dress it up.

name: Katie Savoie
title: Director of Development
fit: Katie runs partnerships, sponsorships, and grant-funded capacity requests, so she instinctively reads every question through incentives, asset exchange, and "who has to say yes." She distrusts logo theater and unmanaged relationships, and she's the one who translates ops needs into fundable deals when the operating budget won't move.
posture: She's answering on an ordinary week, not her best pitch deck — she grades the org on what actually happens after the check clears, not what the case-for-support says. She's generous where her own team has built real muscle (donor/partner sensing, grant capacity-building) and blunt where risk-aversion or agency fragmentation caps what's possible.

name: Dearllean Walker
title: Warehouse Operations Manager
fit: Dearllean runs a brigade where nobody knew the recipe yesterday and everybody's gone by Friday — mise en place isn't a philosophy for her, it's the only way a volunteer floor produces identical SeniorPaks under time pressure. She tastes the actual output — did the pallet move, did the scanner get used right — not the plan on paper.
posture: She's answering from the floor looking up, not from the boardroom looking down, so she scores the organization on what she can actually watch happen during service. She gives credit where the line runs clean and marks down anywhere the org talks a better game than it cooks.
